extracted.intended_audience: beginning users of the computer algebra system Singular (students, mathematicians, researchers) who want a short introduction to using and programming in Singular
extracted.subtask_description: A short hands-on introduction to basic usage, scripting, procedures, libraries, data types, and common commands in the computer algebra system Singular. Covers interactive use, editing, I/O, ring and data-type setup, control structures, and recommended editor integration (ESingular/Emacs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Command termination with semicolon
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, every command in Singular ends with a semicolon!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The semicolon tells the computer that the input is to be interpreted and, if successful, be carried out. If the semicolon is omitted Singular shows an input prompt '.' and allows further inputs (e.g. the missing semicolon) so long commands can be stretched over several lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting and terminating Singular
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular is started by the command 'Singular' on the system command line; termination is done with exit;, quit; or $.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After start Singular shows prompt '>' and is available for interactive use. Note semicolons are part of the commands. '$' is a shorthand for quitting for very lazy users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the online help (help / ?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the command help (or ?) followed by a command, function, procedure name or library to get documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For libraries you receive a list of procedures contained there; for commands/functions/procedures you get purpose, syntax and examples. By default an internet browser opens showing the handbook. Examples: help exit; help standard.lib; help printf;

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrupting Singular (CTRL-C options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Unix-like systems and Windows, CTRL-C forces an interruption and offers options to handle the current operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After CTRL-C the options are: 'a' (Singular carries out the current command and returns to top level), 'c' (Singular carries on), 'q' (Singular is terminated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing inputs and command history (key bindings & completion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular records a history of commands and supports editing previous inputs using key combinations and automatic completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key bindings include TAB for automatic completion of function and file names; arrow keys and CTRL-{A,E,B,F,N,P} to move through/edit lines; BACKSPACE/DEL/CTRL-D for deletion; CTRL-K/CTRL-U to delete to end/beginning of line; RETURN sends the current line to the Singular parser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures are defined with: proc PROCEDURENAME [PARAMETERLIST] { PROCEDUREBODY } where the PARAMETERLIST should be in round brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter types and names are specified in the parameter list (e.g., proc permcol (matrix A, int c1, int c2) { ... }). Procedures are invoked by their name with arguments in parentheses. The proc keyword should appear at the beginning of a new line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure return conventions and local scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If a procedure returns a result, store it in a variable 'result' and finish with return(result);. Variables defined within a procedure are local to that procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local variables may have the same names as outside objects. Example: a procedure that exchanges two matrix columns returns a matrix stored in B and returns it with return(B); (result can be any variable name but convention in text uses result).

rubrics_metrics.name: Library files (.lib) and loading libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures can be stored in files with extension .lib and loaded via LIB "name.lib";
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library names should, if possible, only consist of eight letters for compatibility with systems like DOS. Non-builtin libraries should be in the subdirectory from which Singular is started. Example: LIB "matrix.lib";

rubrics_metrics.name: Library head: version, info and PROCEDURES listing
rubrics_metrics.description: A library should begin with a head containing 'version' and an 'info' string; under PROCEDURES: list procedure names with one-line descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example head includes version="1.0"; info="..."; The info string is shown when help is called on the library (help linalgeb.lib;). Strings are assigned with = and must be enclosed in quotes and terminated by semicolons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library example blocks and help for procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures stored in libraries should include a commentary block (in quotes) with USAGE:, RETURN:, NOTE:, EXAMPLE:, and an example section initiated with the reserved name example which contains runnable Singular code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commentary block’s information is displayed by help PROCEDURENAME; The example section can be shown to the user by entering example PROCEDURENAME;.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment syntax (single-line // and quoted blocks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A double slash // starts a comment that continues to the end of the line; quoted strings can be used as documentation blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use // for inline comments. In libraries, larger documentation (info, and procedure commentary) is placed in quoted strings following reserved keywords like info or immediately after proc (for USAGE/RETURN/EXAMPLE fields).

rubrics_metrics.name: File I/O: write, read, execute, and shorthand '<'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use write("file", vars...) to write variable values or strings to a file; read("file") reads file contents as strings; execute(read("file")) evaluates Singular code stored in a file. A short form for execute(read(...)) is < "file";
rubrics_metrics.guidance: write converts variable values to strings; multiple variables/strings are written line by line. Example: write("hallo.txt",a,b); execute(read("hallo.txt")); or < "hallo.txt";

rubrics_metrics.name: Session logging with monitor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use monitor("filename","options") to record a session to a file; options like 'io' record input and output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: monitor("hallo.txt","io") stores both input and output. Omitting one letter records only input or output. monitor opens a file but does not close it; close by monitor(""); monitor is useful when Singular is unstable on the OS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must define ring before performing computations
rubrics_metrics.description: To perform computations in Singular it is absolutely necessary to define the ring (base ring and ordering) over which work is done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most data types depend on a meta structure, the base ring. Examples: ring r=0,(x),lp; ring r=(0,a,b),(x,y,z),dp; ring r=(real,15),x,ls; ring r=5,x,ds; See the handbook for more ring types and meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring specification: coefficient field, variables and term ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Rings are specified with a coefficient field (e.g., 0 for Q, real,n for floating), a list of variables, and an ordering (lp, dp, ls, ds etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in text: ring r=0,x(0..2),lp; (polynomial ring in x(0),x(1),x(2) with rational coefficients and lex order) and ring r=(0,a),(x,y),lp; (coefficients are rational functions in a and b). Choose appropriate ordering and coefficient ring before computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data types and examples (int, string, intvec, intmat, poly, ideal, qring, map, module, def, list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular provides a variety of data types (int, string, intvec, intmat, number, list, matrix, vector, proc, poly, ideal, qring, map, module, def, link, resolution) and examples show their construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: int i=1; string s="Hallo"; intvec iv=1,2,3; intmat im[2][3]=1,2,3,4,5,6; poly f=x2+2x+1; ideal i=f,x3; qring Q=i; map g=R,x; Use 'def' for unspecified types whose type is inferred at first assignment. Consult handbook for link and resolution types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and allocations (use of '=')
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator '=' assigns values to variables; assignment can be done at declaration or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: int i=1; or int i; ... i=2; The operator is used consistently for setting variable values and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control structures: for and while loops
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular supports for loops (when number of iterations is known) and while loops (when unknown); loop bodies are in curly braces, control in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For-loop format: for (init; condition; update) { ... } Example: for (i=1; i<=10; i=i+1) { s=s+i; } While: while (condition) { ... } The termination condition is checked before the first entry into a while loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branching: if-else syntax and blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular uses if (condition) { ... } else { ... } where the else part is optional; blocks are enclosed in curly braces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if (i<5 or s<10) { s=5; } else { s=0; } Conditions are in parentheses; commands in curly braces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison and boolean operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality and inequality use '==' and '!=' (or '<>'); relational operators <, >, <=, >= are available for int, number, poly and vector; boolean connectives are 'and', 'or', and 'not'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: '==' returns 1 if equal and 0 otherwise. Examples: not ((1==0) or (1!=0)); 7 div 3; 7 mod 3; For some data types consult handbook for operator behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-specific operators (int, list, matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators may depend on data type: integers use +, -, *, ^, div, mod; lists support + (concatenate), delete(L,i), insert(L,elem[,pos]); matrices support +, -, * and indexing/ slicing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matrix element access examples: m[1,2]; m[1,1..3]; m[1..2,3]; print(m) shows layout. Use provided functions (ncols, nrows, transpose, det) and library routines (permrow, permcol, gauss_row, rowred, etc.) for matrix operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix and linear-algebra related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular core and libraries provide many matrix/linear algebra functions such as ncols, nrows, print, size, transpose, det, and library functions permrow, permcol, multrow, multcol, addrow, addcol, concat, unitmat, gauss_row, gauss_col, rowred, colred; pmat in inout.lib for pretty printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use help or the handbook for syntax details. Example libraries: matrix.lib and inout.lib (pmat). The tutorial lists commonly used functions for convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESingular / Emacs integration recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Emacs (or Xemacs) and ESingular mode for writing Singular procedures and libraries to benefit from syntax highlighting, menus and editor features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start ESingular with ESingular --emacs=xemacs or set EMACS environment variable to change editor. ESingular runs Singular inside Emacs, offering pulldown menus and options that simplify editing and error correction, useful especially for inexperienced users.
